title: RoboLoc-G: Multisensor Localization Dataset from a Robotic Gantry System

keys: RoboLoc-G: Multisensor Localization Dataset from a Robotic Gantry System

rights: CC BY 4.0 per Zenodo metadata. Attribute the named depositors. Only new summaries, references and independent readers are included; original archives remain available at source.
queries: Zenodo / DataCite query "Wi-Fi FTM" and following the prior G1 FTM frame derivative; obtained additional independent gantry, motion capture and original ROS2 archives from fixed record 15989282.
Archive data manual: RoboLoc-G.pdf pp. 3–4 for anchor/tag geometry, p. 6 for generated ground truth and Chrony time shift, pp. 7–9 for ROS2 topics and units.
evidence_grade: Upgrade to an existing fixed release. Complete primary files with separate optical/gantry streams and MCAP records. Historical G1 already checked within-frame timestamp double differences; those frames are not counted as new data.
clock: All 8 mobile-tag MCAPs were parsed using uncompressed MCAP chunk/channel/message records and little-endian CDR. Matched all physical FTM frames (anchor, estimates, num_frames, array order, RSSI, RTT and t1–t4) as well as UWB anchor/tag/range/sequence to numeric CSV. CSV timestamp matches the MCAP log_time for every session. None occurs in the publish_time set of the same take and topic. The MCAP separation reflects recording/publication metadata, not the time of transmission over the radio, nor packet travel time to an actuator.
geometry: Source lists UWB anchor IDs directly; FTM session anchor suffixes are always +1 compared with the four documented suffixes and matched on that explicit assumption. The latter comparison is conditional. Interpolate the gantry-derived tag position at each CSV/MCAP log time; never extrapolate. Endpoints originate from the gantry movement log and calibrated rigid tag offsets. The two ground-truth ZIP tables use two coordinate frames derived from the same gantry motion. One zigzag3 timestamp 1751474938.2291045 s has two distinct positions roughly 142 mm apart; reject that sample and its adjacent interpolation intervals. CSV row alignment to the original gantry export was confirmed within 0.3 microseconds and 1e-9 mm of coordinate serialization rounding.
unit_check: RoboLoc-G.pdf calls UWB range metres. Actual CDR range and numeric CSV are integers 1011–6340. Kept the literal interpretation as a counterexample and explicitly tested a millimetre scale against the independently recorded gantry motion: bracketed take/anchor RMSE for the metre interpretation was about 2979–4223 m, and 0.035–0.320 m after division by 1000. The upload omits a per-packet ISO-traceable reference. Recorded FTM dist_est is in metres. The frames.rtt unit label is already covered by previous G1.
optical: Read actual 120 Hz OptiTrack Grua rigid-body XYZ in its own frame from the 8 Motive exports. Added relative frame time to local capture start (Europe/Madrid; daypart from Take Name), then independently interpolated the gantry-derived Grua in the published optical coordinate frame. Applied shifts -16, 0 and +16 ms on the same finite support for a fair comparison. Six of seven moving takes improve Euclidean RMSE with +16 ms versus zero, while zigzag1 increases from 7.694 to 7.788 mm; the stationary take cannot identify a shift. Optical calibration and tag offsets share sources with the published alignment. These residuals combine spatial calibration, motion and timing.
reproduce: Download the five ZIP files above to RAW. Run python derive_roboloc.py RAW OUT with Python 3.9+, NumPy and Europe/Madrid zoneinfo. Retains negative publish-to-log intervals if observed.
